accepted.question_text: Let A be a P-matrix, meaning that every principal minor A[α] is positive. Call A weakly sign-symmetric when A[α,β]A[β,α] ≥ 0 for every almost principal minor, i.e. for every minor whose dispersal #α − #(α ∩ β) equals 1. Such weakly sign-symmetric P-matrices are called GKK matrices. Call A a strict GKK matrix when the inequalities A[α,β]A[β,α] > 0 hold for all almost principal minors. Let l(A) be the smallest real eigenvalue of A, with l(A)=∞ if A has no real eigenvalues. A matrix is a τ-matrix when it has eigenvalue monotonicity l(A(α,α)) ≤ l(A(β,β)) < ∞ whenever ∅ ≠ β ⊆ α, and in addition l(A) ≥ 0. Which GKK matrices can be approximated arbitrarily well by strict GKK matrices, and in particular can the unstable matrices constructed in Holtz [11] be approximated by τ-matrices that are strict GKK?

Carlson’s theorem [3] asserts that the value d = n is suﬃcient for stability (in other words, that sign- symmetric matrices are stable).
